callGraph.callPath: No allocation or callLocal is transported as Derived through a cyclic component. Its outgoing reachable domain has no actual allocations/views, so every cyclic Derived owner is one of the current function full Array parameter slots. External fresh actuals are substituted only at their finite incoming call. Allocation imports elsewhere follow the acyclic condensation path, at most15 frames; existing maxItems15 is retained. Effective callLocal never enters Derived or a callee Effective recurrence.
callGraph.classification: A component is cyclic iff it has more than one member or a self-edge. Use all functions/ordinary occurrences without export or entry reachability pruning. Pure graph classification does not change owner meter; source cardinalities bound it.
callGraph.coldConsumer: Compute complete caller→callee transitive closure over every represented function including private/unreachable; each cyclic node and every outgoing reachable function must contain no tsfg_array.create. No need to reject incoming acyclic entry allocation. Keep entry fuel1 in each function; Any actual checked-view creation in that cyclic outgoing domain is also rejected, matching existing upstream policy.
callGraph.eligibility: Only for a graph containing a cycle: validate the entire exact selected facts/HIR and fixed context4 identity/slots/upper/digests first. Form the union of every cyclic SCC and its complete outgoing reachable functions. Every function in this union must use only required Array<f64>/f64/u32 parameters, f64 results, prior Array aliases and existing checked read/store/resize/ordinary calls. Reject any actual local fresh Array literal, any ReadSpan parameter/result/local/use in that union. The restriction is transitive and includes unreachable SCCs. An outside caller may pass its own fresh owner into this domain. Published.local true is not evidence of actual fresh syntax and is allowed.
callGraph.fixedContext: A complete graph containing any cycle requires fixed context4 at all nine public seams, even without actual views. Missing/invalid fixed preparation base or identity maps to r03-array-hir-context at the five HIR seams, while the four ArrayCalls seams retain original base/identity. A complete no-view DAG retains the existing optional two-argument HIR route.

denseStaticProof.credit: no checks removed by this proof; no execution, physical storage, alias escape, general static safety or Main25 completion
denseStaticProof.domain: per-function exact length or unknown keyed by allocation root; aliases share root. Array parameter roots are permanently unknown, including through aliases, because distinct parameters may alias. Every Array actual at an ordinary call invalidates its caller owner length knowledge; no interprocedural length hint or optimistic read-only inference.
denseStaticProof.failure: Source private located static semantic rejection at original index/newLength expression; cold self-consistent packets and Core must independently reject proven literal gap/growth; all parameter/unknown states retain future reach-time checks
denseStaticProof.initial: new literal establishes exact element count; alias retains the original root and its current state, not a copied state snapshot
denseStaticProof.read: do not evaluate reads or RHS, do not reject/fold OOB reads, propagate caller constants, infer intervals or execute values; this is a proof of selected source dense invariants, not a guest interpreter
denseStaticProof.resize: for original literal newLength N and exact length L, reject N>L as statically proven uninitialized growth; otherwise on normal continuation set exact N. Literal resize from unknown also sets exact N only on normal continuation; its check remains. Parameter resize sets unknown. Any parameter-derived owner remains unknown even after literal resize.
denseStaticProof.store: for an original literal index and exact length L, reject index>L as a statically proven gap; index==L is allowed append and sets exact L+1 on normal continuation; index<L retains exact L. A parameter index sets unknown on normal continuation. Existing checked operation is always retained. An unknown prior length stays unknown for literal store.

readSpanView.calls: Any actual ordinary call strictly after view creation and before its last actual use is outside this first profile and refuses with core-ir-readspan-capability. This obviates an invented view/call ABI or GC root promise; no view parameter/result/alias op.
readSpanView.lifetime: From complete verified actual one-block Core: derive each Array SSA root through real creates/aliases/parameters, derive view owner from its actual checked-create operand, collect real read/length uses and exact last instruction. Never trust supplied HIR plan, local nonStructural boolean or Derived hints. Array parameters may alias each other and never acquire exact length. At every direct store/resize while a may-alias view is active, require cold recomputed existing overwrite / equal-length resize, otherwise reject; RHS view read completion precedes store, so final RHS read can end borrow before append. Zero length does not erase borrow.
readSpanView.normalized: tsfg_array.view_lifetimes optional ArrayAttr input assertion; consumer inserts it whenever views exist, ordered by create instruction, each exact {view_register:i64,owner_register:i64,create_instruction:i64,last_use_instruction:i64}; last use is create itself if unused. Registers include all entry parameters/results in source operation order. Owner is the original Array root SSA, not a new allocation or view SSA.
readSpanView.ranges: checked-create uses owner,start,length, not an end index. start and length retain fullu32 including4294967295; check start<=owner.length and length<=owner.length-start before forming a view, avoiding wrapping addition. Checked read index<=4294967294 and index<view.length before access; retain checks even for empty/equal/far-OOB literal inputs. Static verifier validates types/roles/SSA/ranges, never executes or pretraps.
